summary: Niacin contributes to energy metabolism and normal cell development and function.

functions.title: Physiological role
functions.description: Niacin contributes to energy metabolism and normal cell development and function.

foodSourceRules.notes: USDA niacin mass is not niacin equivalents (NE). Tryptophan contribution is not inferred, and an NE ranking is unavailable.

deficiency.overview: Severe niacin deficiency can lead to pellagra. Low niacin or tryptophan intake and certain medical conditions can contribute.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: High-dose niacin supplements can cause adverse effects, including flushing with nicotinic acid and liver problems with some high-dose regimens.
excess.medicalBoundary: No upper limit is an intake goal. Seek professional or medical advice before changing supplement or medication use.

interactions.counterparty: Medicines discussed in the linked NIH ODS fact sheet
interactions.description: High-dose nicotinic acid can affect blood glucose and interfere with diabetes medicines. Prescription niacin use requires clinical supervision.
interactions.limitations: Informational summary, not a complete interaction list or an instruction to change medicines.
